title: Index laws
examples: When do I need to use the index laws?
Can I use these laws with variables?
What is the difference between a negative and a fractional index?

explain.say: Today we are learning about index laws. These laws help us simplify expressions with exponents. Remember that an index tells us how many times to multiply a number by itself.
When multiplying powers with the same base, we add the indices. For example, two to the power of three times two to the power of two equals two to the power of five.

items: Multiply powers same base: a^m imes a^n

explain.say: When dividing powers with the same base, we subtract the indices. Try simplifying three to the power of seven divided by three to the power of three. The answer is three to the power of four.

items: Divide powers same base: a^m / a^n

explain.say: A negative index means we take the reciprocal. For example, two to the power of negative one is one divided by two to the power of one. So, two to the power of negative one equals one over two.
A fractional index means taking a root. For instance, two to the power of one over two is the square root of two. This is because the denominator tells us the root.

draw.text: $a^{1/n} = ext{the } n ext{-th root of } a$

faq.q: What does it mean to have a negative index?
faq.a: It means you take the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive index. For example, five to the power of negative two is one over twenty-five.
asks: What is the rule for negative exponents?
How do I handle a negative index?

faq.q: How do I work with fractional indices?
faq.a: The denominator of the fraction tells you which root to take. For example, three to the power of one over three is the cube root of three.
asks: What does the denominator mean in an index?
Can I use roots with fractional indices?

faq.q: Do I always add or subtract when multiplying and dividing?
faq.a: Yes, when the bases are the same, you add the indices for multiplication and subtract them for division. This is a key rule to remember.
asks: What do I do with the powers when I multiply?
Is it always addition or subtraction?

faq.q: Does the base have to be the same for these laws to work?
faq.a: Yes, the base must be identical for you to use the simple addition or subtraction rules. You cannot combine different bases like two to the power of three and three to the power of two directly.
asks: Can I mix bases in these laws?
What if the bases are different?

faq.q: What if the power is zero?
faq.a: Any non-zero number raised to the power of zero is equal to one. For example, seven to the power of zero is one.
asks: What is any number to the power of zero?

facts: When multiplying powers with the same base, you add the indices.
When dividing powers with the same base, you subtract the indices.
A negative index indicates the reciprocal of the base raised to the positive index.
A fractional index represents taking a root of the base.

quiz.why: When multiplying powers with the same base, you add the indices, so five plus three equals eight.

wrong.1: This is a common mistake because students sometimes multiply the indices instead of adding them.
wrong.2: This happens if a student incorrectly multiplies the bases and the indices together.
wrong.3: This confuses the multiplication rule with the division rule.

quiz.why: A negative index means taking the reciprocal, so five to the power of negative two is one over five squared, which is one over twenty-five.

wrong.1: This mistake treats the negative index as a negative sign in front of the result.
wrong.2: This incorrectly adds the negative index to the base.
wrong.3: This mistake ignores the negative sign entirely and calculates the positive power.

quiz.why: When raising a power to another power, you multiply the indices together, so two times three equals six.

wrong.0: This incorrectly adds the indices, which is the rule for multiplication, not for a power of a power.
wrong.1: This incorrectly divides the indices by the outer power.
wrong.2: This mistake fails to apply the outer exponent to the entire base.
